headline: Ten minutes from everything, with the mountain out.
lede: Bonney Lake sits along SR-410 in Pierce County, between Sumner and the Cascade foothills, with Lake Tapps at its north end and Tehaleh to the south. Here is what an ordinary week here actually looks like, from a local agent who knows it first-hand.

chapters.title: From a local agent, first-hand
chapters.intro: We’re a busy family with young kids in sports. These are the places we actually go, and the ones I send everyone to.
items: My food pick: George’s Bonney Lake Tavern, right off 410. Same owner as Al Lago and the Island Lodge. Very, very good food, fun places to be.
Our sushi place in Bonney Lake. We like eating there.
Locally owned and very good, right next to Kohl’s. There are also Starbucks everywhere: two right off 410, one inside Fred Meyer (overkill) and one inside Safeway. They’re all good.
A very fun one to go to, and where local families and dog owners love to be. My favorite field is actually over at Allan Yorke, because they just opened up the soccer and baseball fields.
Down to Victor Falls on the trails. It can be a little dicey in the winter, but it’s a good one.
Post & Pour, a short drive away
If you’re willing to take a quick drive into Tehaleh, grab a coffee or a flatbread at Post & Pour, overlooking the mountain. Very fun, very nice. And if you’re a member, The Mantel.
We are a busy family with young kids in sports, so we also have to say Chipotle, because it’s quick.

chapters.title: A day in the life
chapters.kicker: A Saturday in Bonney Lake, the way we live it
chapters.sig: on a Saturday in Bonney Lake
chapters.intro: If you’re an active person, Bonney Lake makes the morning easy: a walk, a park, a jog, then coffee. Here’s how a good Saturday goes for us.
moments: Out for a walk, a jog, a park

There are parks and trails all around. Which ones become yours depends on where you live and how you like to spend a morning. Some of the best aren’t obvious; you have to live here and get a feel for your style.
Lamppost, or one of four Starbucks
Lamppost by Kohl’s is the local one, and it’s very good. Or pick a Starbucks. You won’t have to look hard.
It’s not a super updated theater, but it’s a good one to catch newer movies in because it isn’t packed. Most people go to the nicer theaters with the comfy chairs.
Glow Martini Lounge is right there if you want a drink beforehand, with plenty of restaurants around it if you want to sit down.
Al Lago, the Island Lodge, or the BLT
We love Al Lago, which is technically Lake Tapps but so close to Bonney Lake, and the Island Lodge by Al Lago. The BLT is right off 410. All the same owner, all very good.
If you live near Lake Tapps, we love watching the sunset over the water. If you don’t, there are plenty of viewpoints to catch it and walk around.
honest: What people don’t realize until they live here

The 410 commute really isn’t that bad. It’s the 167-to-410 interchange that slows you down. And errands are easy: you’re 10 to 15 minutes from almost anywhere in Bonney Lake to Costco, Target or Fred Meyer, so you get things done fast.

Someone who expects a 10-minute commute. Most people here commute, usually 30 to 45 minutes each way, sometimes more. And if date night means a small family-owned Italian or Mexican place, there are a few very good ones, but a lot of what’s here is chains. People often head to Sumner, Enumclaw, Puyallup or Tacoma for date night.

chapters.title: Where kids and dogs go
chapters.intro: Allan Yorke Park is the answer most of the time. It sits on the south end of Lake Tapps, and nearly everything a family wants on a summer day is in one place.
items: Ball fields, a covered beach area with barbecues, swimming areas, a fishing dock, playgrounds, a skate park, tennis and volleyball courts, trails, a snack shack and kayak and paddleboard rentals. 7203 West Tapps Highway E; closes at dusk.
A multi-sport turf field built for baseball, soccer, lacrosse and rugby.
The city built a new playground at Allan Yorke and held its celebration in September 2025, alongside a welcome-home parade for the Bonney Lake–Sumner Little League.
The city’s off-leash dog park, at 18902 82nd St E.

The city bought this 3.25-acre property in 2013 to give people a safe place to see the falls. Today it has a falls viewpoint, soft-surface paths, picnic tables, barbecues and parking at 18212 Rhodes Lake Rd E. Closes at dusk.

chapters.title: Lake Tapps and the boat launch
chapters.intro: Summer on Lake Tapps is a big part of life here, and it gets busy. Plan for it.
items: Allan Yorke boat launch: residents only in 2026

For the 2026 season the city opened its launch to Bonney Lake residents only, with a trailer parking pass of $40 plus tax ($43.80) per vehicle per year. It opens when Cascade Water Alliance says the lake is at recreational levels, and closes at dusk. The rule can change from year to year, so check before you tow.

Pierce County’s park on the north end has a boat ramp and is open to the public first-come, first-served. The launch is typically closed November through March, and it closed early in August 2026 because of drought.
Launching can be difficult on a busy day. It helps to know somebody with private launch access, like a friend on Tapps Island or someone with their own launch. — Chris

chapters.title: Errands, and how it compares
chapters.intro: Bonney Lake’s main corridor runs along SR-410, which is why errands go fast.
items: At 9801 204th Ave E, with gas and a tire center. “One of the best Costcos in the area: multiple exits, multiple entrances. I talk about it all the time. It makes me feel like an old person, but that is a wonderful Costco.” — Chris
Tehaleh is a planned community at Bonney Lake’s south end. Next to it, Bonney Lake feels much bigger and more spread out, with a lot more history. — Chris

Sumner is very close, and much more of a cute downtown. Bonney Lake is cute too: you’re overlooking the mountain, there are wonderful places to live and great schools. It’s just more spread out. — Chris

faq: What is it like to live in Bonney Lake, WA?

In Chris Ranch’s experience, it’s an easy place to be active and get things done: parks and trails all around, Lake Tapps in summer, and Costco, Target and Fred Meyer 10 to 15 minutes from almost anywhere in town. It’s more spread out than Sumner, with Mount Rainier views and a lot of history.
How bad is the commute from Bonney Lake?
Most people commute, usually 30 to 45 minutes each way and sometimes more. In Chris’s experience, SR-410 itself isn’t bad; the 167-to-410 interchange is what slows you down.
Can non-residents use the Allan Yorke Park boat launch?

Not in 2026. The city opened the launch to Bonney Lake residents only, with a $43.80 yearly trailer parking pass, and it opens when the lake reaches recreational levels. Pierce County’s North Lake Tapps Park has a public boat ramp, typically closed November through March. Rules change by season, so check before you go.
boating
Is there a Costco in Bonney Lake?
Yes, at 9801 204th Ave E, with gas and a tire center. Chris calls it one of the best Costcos in the area, with multiple entrances and exits.
costco
Where do families and dog owners go in Bonney Lake?

Allan Yorke Park on Lake Tapps first: swimming areas, playgrounds, a skate park, ball fields including a multi-sport turf field, and trails. Viking Park is the city’s off-leash dog park, and Victor Falls Park has a falls viewpoint and soft-surface paths (Chris notes the trails can be dicey in winter).
ayp
Are there good restaurants in Bonney Lake?

There are a few very good local ones. Chris’s picks are George’s Bonney Lake Tavern (the BLT) off 410, Trapper’s Sushi, and Al Lago and the Island Lodge just over in Lake Tapps. A lot of what’s on 410 is chains, so for date night many people head to Sumner, Enumclaw, Puyallup or Tacoma.
How is Bonney Lake different from Tehaleh?
Tehaleh is a planned community at Bonney Lake’s south end, built around its own trails and parks. In Chris’s experience, Bonney Lake as a whole feels bigger and more spread out, with more history.
tehwiki
How is Bonney Lake different from Sumner?
Sumner is very close and is much more of a cute downtown area. Bonney Lake is more spread out, with Mount Rainier views and quick access to Lake Tapps and the big-box errands along SR-410.
Who is Bonney Lake not a good fit for?
Someone who expects a 10-minute commute, or who wants lots of small, family-owned restaurants close by. Most residents commute 30 to 45 minutes each way.
How many people live in Bonney Lake?
22,487 at the 2020 census. Bonney Lake incorporated as a town in 1949.
blwiki
Is there a movie theater in Bonney Lake?
Yes. Regal Tall Firs 10, at 20751 SR-410 E, opened in 1997. Chris likes it for newer movies because it isn’t packed.
